scope: Question-only endpoint designs for independent observed-data workflow adaptations; no benchmark answers, fixtures or exact-answer reproduction. Nearby broad question IDs are navigation, not equivalence claims.
design_principles: One coherent observed-data task per recipe by default. These refine the 147 broad questions; do not add design counts across planning levels.

Pin each independent study accession, release, license, checksum, native file formats, biological dimensions and every subset transformation. Source paper/accession identifiers listed here are exclusions, not proposed training sources.
Freeze complete schemas, numerical tolerances, package versions and offline annotation snapshots before implementation. Proposed artifact columns are not complete validated schemas.
Run the actual package reference plus independent input/artifact invariants. Negative controls corrupt outputs against fixed observations; no assumption that random labels must change significance.

Question inspection cannot recover omitted source methods. Ambiguous or scientifically invalid source formulations remain explicit gaps; a corrected authored task is a method adaptation, not exact endpoint equivalence.

All designs still need independent input selection, native oracle/verifier runs, incorrect-output checks and measured offline runtime at most 30 minutes. No release readiness or coverage forecast is implied.

method_references.use: Unnormalized counts or valid quantified-count import; full-rank model and shrinkage/contrast semantics.
Equivalence requires bounds and an equivalence test; nonsignificant difference is not an equivalence result.
Native metric entry points; pinned implementation details still require per-metric reconciliation.

ortholog_signal_contract.execution_protocol: Harbor only; no notebook protocol. This specification creates no runnable task or coverage credit.

wheel_source_verification.result: All 11 reviewed files match both their pinned Git tree blobs and downloaded PhyKIT 2.7.0 wheel members. This is source identity evidence, not new native execution.

data.interpretation: A/B replace the source animal/fungal groups with two explicitly named animal clades; taxonomic study equivalence is not claimed. Original orthogroups are the locus units. Candidate rights and benchmark lineage are not cleared.
data.paired_units: One retained alignment/tree per original orthogroup and clade. Both clades share each locus; retain all eligibility and exclusion rows.
data.named_loci: Order original orthogroup IDs lexically before computing outcomes. Positions 1, 2, 3 and 4 define named_locus_dvmc, named_locus_lb, named_locus_distance and named_locus_rate, respectively. Record the resolved IDs in the public manifest.
data.five_tree_panel: The five lexically first original orthogroup IDs in clade A, selected before outcomes. This is the exact denominator for the five-tree endpoint, not all 30 loci or all 60 trees.

tree_preparation.rooting: Prune using DendroPy 5.0.8, preserve distances while suppressing unifurcations, then midpoint-root with the audited DendroPy path. Midpoint is a geometric convention, not an inferred biological ancestor. Serialize the root edge as zero.
tree_preparation.branch_rules: Retain input precision and original identifiers; reject negative/nonfinite lengths, duplicate tips or mismatched alignment/tree taxon sets. An omitted root length becomes zero; missing non-root lengths are invalid. No outcome-based locus dropping.
checks: Every original retained pairwise distance equals its pruned and rooted distance within the numerical contract.
Root-to-tip depth along a diameter equals half the original diameter; all tips and alignment rows have exact matching identities.

alignment_rules.alphabet: Uppercase observed amino-acid alignments. Preserve native gaps and masked symbols; reject unknown non-ASCII symbols. Flag observed B/Z/J/U/O rather than silently converting them.
alignment_rules.asparagine: N is a protein residue, not missing DNA. Every native calculation must use protein mode.
alignment_rules.gap_percent: 100 * literal hyphen cells / (n_taxa * alignment_columns). Report the wider native missing-symbol fraction separately. The source question does not define gap-versus-missing convention; this is an explicit authored choice.
alignment_rules.columns: Keep the original aligned columns after clade subsetting, including all-gap columns. Do not silently retrim separately per clade.
alignment_rules.source_adaptation: Native PhyKIT counts nonexcluded ambiguity letters as states. Report both native results and a canonical-20-amino-acid sensitivity result when B/Z/J/U/O occur; do not label the two as identical estimands.

metrics.tree_length: Sum every branch length on the processed tree, including a root edge fixed to zero.
metrics.treeness: Sum nonterminal branch lengths / total tree length on the same processed tree; undefined when total length is zero.
metrics.evolutionary_rate: Total tree length / number of terminal taxa. This is a branch-length summary, not a time-calibrated evolutionary rate.
metrics.dvmc: Sample SD (ddof=1) of terminal root-to-tip distances; no division by the mean. Across-locus SD of these DVMC values is a separate aggregation.
metrics.patristic: One row for each unordered distinct-tip pair. Locus mean/median use all n*(n-1)/2 pairs, with no self-distances or reciprocal duplicates.
metrics.lb_native: Use the pinned native long-branch implementation and preserve its historical taxon-name denominator. For candidate multi-character IDs without single-character tip collisions, each tip mean includes its zero self-distance and divides by n. Score is 100*(tip_mean/global_unordered_pair_mean - 1). Audit names before using this simplification.
metrics.lb_self_excluded: Separately report 100*(sum of distances to other tips/(n-1)/global_unordered_pair_mean - 1). Do not silently substitute it for native LB. Across-tip mean is zero up to numerical precision; native mean is -100/n under the stated identifier condition.
metrics.informative: A column is informative when at least two nonexcluded states each occur at least twice. Count all columns in the denominator; informative_percent=100*informative_count/alignment_columns.
metrics.rcv: For sequence i and each nonexcluded observed symbol a, count c_ia; let cbar_a be the mean count over n sequences and L_i the nonexcluded length. Native RCV is sum_i(sum_a(abs(c_ia-cbar_a))/(n*L_i)); a zero-L_i sequence contributes zero. This is not composition frequencies normalized to a common aligned length.
metrics.saturation: Use native gap-excluded pair distances: y is mismatch count divided by positions where both sequences lack native missing symbols; x is patristic distance. Fit through the origin with slope=sum(x*y)/sum(x*x) over finite pairs. Retain slope and abs(1-slope); the authored saturation endpoint uses abs(1-slope). It is not a free-intercept regression or Pearson correlation.
metrics.treeness_over_rcv: Divide unrounded treeness by unrounded RCV for each matched alignment/tree, then summarize ratios. Undefined when RCV is zero; never replace it with an infinite or zero score.

aggregation_rules.input_precision: Authored endpoints use unrounded native API values or independently audited full-precision formulas, with at least 12 significant digits retained. Native CLI outputs are additional evidence at their documented display precision. Source CLI rounding may induce different ties; this is an explicit precision adaptation, not a claim of exact source answers.
aggregation_rules.sd_variance: Across-locus SD and variance use ddof=1. n<2 gives insufficient_observations. Source wording does not resolve ddof; the authored task states this choice.
aggregation_rules.quantiles: Median and 75th percentile use NumPy 2.2.6 method=linear. Thresholds use unrounded values and the written strict > or < comparison.
aggregation_rules.mann_whitney: SciPy 1.15.3 mannwhitneyu(A,B,alternative=two-sided,method=asymptotic,use_continuity=True). Return U for A. Independently reconstruct U using average pooled ranks; use the native tie-corrected p-value and report n_A, n_B and tie groups.
aggregation_rules.interpretation: Matched clade loci are dependent; Mann-Whitney is retained only as a descriptive source-requested calculation. Its p-value must not be presented as valid independent-samples evidence about clade differences. Complete paired differences are a separate required artifact.
aggregation_rules.directions: Differences and fold ratios mean B-A and B/A unless the endpoint explicitly uses abs. A ratio of medians and the median of paired ratios remain different columns.
aggregation_rules.weighting: Compute tip/pair summaries within each locus first, then use equally weighted loci. Do not pool tips/pairs across loci. Retain every denominator and eligible-locus identity.
aggregation_rules.undefined: Keep rows with reason codes: zero_denominator, empty_selection, insufficient_observations or no_comparable_sites. Numeric value is null, not NaN/Inf or an invented zero. Summaries report total, eligible and excluded counts. Require a nonempty eligible set for a numerical endpoint.
aggregation_rules.saturation_degeneracy: Zero comparable sites makes a pair unavailable. If no finite pairs remain or sum(x*x)=0, the scientific slope is undefined. Preserve the native zero-slope fallback only in an audit field, not as evidence of saturation.
aggregation_rules.rounding: Only explicitly rounded endpoint displays use decimal ROUND_HALF_EVEN (three decimals for bix-35-q4 and integer for bix-60-q1). Retain the unrounded calculation in a separate column.

independent_checks: Reconstruct branch/path sums with a second parser and compare all pairs.
Count informative sites, symbol counts and eligible pair positions independently from FASTA.

ora.statistics: For each eligible term report N=background size, K=term genes in background, n=selected genes in background and k=overlap; audit the hypergeometric upper tail P[X>=k]. Preserve native p.adjust and the exact set of hypotheses over which it was computed.

Such rows retain native_not_returned or size_excluded; do not silently append p=1 rows and change the native BH denominator. A separately named all-eligible BH sensitivity analysis may be supplied but cannot replace native results.
ora.semantic_simplification: For each view simplify the native BP results passing padj<0.05, with cutoff=0.7,by=p.adjust,select_fun=min,measure=Wang and a pinned species-compatible semData. Preserve native term order, the full similarity matrix and a before/after retained-ID table.
ora.semantic_ties: The inspected clusterProfiler 4.18.4 source resolves equal selected values using the greatest number of ontology ancestors, then the first tied entry. It loops through local similarity neighborhoods and unions removals; this is not connected-component clustering or a guarantee of one surviving representative per removed term. Do not invent a one-to-one representative map.
ora.native_input_boundary: Convert IDs to unique character vectors. Explicitly set options(enrichment_force_universe=FALSE). DOSE computes n from annotation-mapped query genes before restricting term overlaps to the supplied universe, so passing out-of-background query genes can corrupt the intended denominator.
ora.native_hypothesis_family: DOSE constructs candidate terms from the supplied annotation-mapped query genes, then intersects their memberships with the effective universe and filters by minGSSize/maxGSSize before BH adjustment. Under the explicit pre-intersection rule every native tested term has nonzero overlap. Export those exact tested IDs and all eligible zero-overlap terms separately; do not include appended zero-overlap rows in native BH correction.
ora.qvalue_policy: Set seed 42 immediately before each ORA call because DOSE invokes qvalue with pi0.method=bootstrap. Export its result/status separately; deterministic acceptance and term selection use native BH p.adjust, not Storey qvalue. ora.semantic_graph: Use the checksum-pinned GOSemSim 2.36.0 bundled gotbl.rda for Wang similarity and the separately pinned GO.db 3.22.0 ancestors for clusterProfiler tie-breaking.
